runbooks.diagnosis: Stalwart listener flapping in this stack is typically a port collision (another container or the host claims 25/465/587/993) or a config reload loop where the listener references a certificate that fails to load, making the listener bounce.
remediation: Check stalwart logs for the specific listener bind error
Verify certificate files exist and are readable for the listener's TLS config
Confirm no port conflict with the host or other containers
Restart stalwart only after the cause is fixed — blind restarts churn the flap

runbooks.diagnosis: Credential source mismatch: Stalwart's auth directory must point at the same user store the client expects (Zitadel OIDC or internal). After an IdM change, cached IMAP sessions keep old tokens while new ones fail.
remediation: Check which auth mechanism the failing client uses
Verify the Stalwart directory config matches the current IdM
Clear stale sessions by restarting the affected account's connection, not the server

runbooks.diagnosis: Outbound relay refused: the smarthost/relay config or SPF-related rejection. In this stack outbound mail goes through the configured relay; a wrong relay host yields 554 on submission.
remediation: Inspect the queue for the failing recipient domain
Verify relay host credentials and network reachability
Check the rejection reason before changing DNS/SPF

runbooks.diagnosis: Stalwart (directory=oidc) validates every token via http://$ZITADEL_DOMAIN:8081/..., resolved by the fleet pin to host-gateway :8081 (host traefik). ufw INPUT DROP blocks container→host :8081, so userinfo calls hang: IMAP AUTHENTICATE XOAUTH2 times out, POST /api/account/auth (app passwords) 401s, and stale sessions report 'access token invalid'.
remediation: Allow the container subnet to reach host port 8081/tcp in ufw (comment 'opensme idpplain backchannel (stalwart userinfo)')
Persist the rule in the ansible web_hosts firewall role (mirrors the tinyproxy 8888 precedent)
Re-test XOAUTH2 login and app-password minting (scripts/stalwart-app-password.sh)

runbooks.diagnosis: Stalwart principals auto-provision on first SSO login — on fresh stacks only a few users (e.g. testuser) have real mailboxes, so multi-recipient SMTP to others fails with 550. Also only app passwords work on IMAP (OIDC directory; demo passwords refused).
remediation: Send per-recipient best-effort: deliver to existing mailboxes, report the missing ones
Never rely on a single multi-recipient message; a 550 kills the whole submission
Delivering evidence: server log from=..., to=[...], code=250 + 'Delivery completed'

runbooks.diagnosis: A single message with ~14 RCPTs makes Stalwart drop the SMTP session ('Connection unexpectedly closed'); a fresh TCP connect per recipient adds ~4.5s each (14 serial ≈ 65s).
remediation: Per-recipient sends with ~5 parallel workers (~5s total)
Give the client a generous timeout (SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS 60s)
Log per-recipient delivery, not one big transaction

runbooks.diagnosis: A sending domain without DMARC alignment gets the test invoice filed to Junk by Stalwart's spam filter. Intake relies on a sieve 'fileinto' rule to a local INvoices folder (server-managed sieve; Stalwart 0.15 has no automount).
remediation: Install the sieve rule via the Stalwart admin API (--print-sieve from scripts/paperless-intake.sh)
Whitelist / fix SPF·DKIM·DMARC for the sending domain, or verify messages landed out of Junk before relying on intake
Check the Junk folder first when 'delivery completed' but no document appears
